title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 72
paragraphs: These gained the greatest renown of those who fought at Plataea. As for Callicrates — the handsomest man to come to the camp, not only of the Lacedaemonians but of all the Greeks of his time — he was not killed in the battle itself; but while Pausanias was offering sacrifice, he was struck by an arrow in the side as he was sitting in his place in the ranks. While the rest were fighting, he, having been carried out of the ranks, was dying a lingering death. He said to Arimnestos, a Plataean, that it did not grieve him to die for Greece, but only that he had not proved his strength of hand, and that no deed of valor had been performed by him worthy of the spirit he had in him to perform great deeds.
